=================== #2016
TITLE: Write-wave root arm signs a commitment without a cut-epoch floor read
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: v2-build,comp:engine,post-cutover
MILESTONE: post-cutover

## Problem

The root arm of the write wave signs a commitment without a read of the cut-epoch floor. `WriteWaveNet::publish_moved` in `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs` reads the read-epoch floor and the write-epoch floor, then calls `reseal_root`, which re-signs `authorized_commitment` with no cut-epoch floor read.

Every other owner publish path reaches the check. The grant-edit publishes (append, invite, permission change, rename, conversion) go through `OwnerRotationNet::publish_scope_root` and `RootPublish::run`, which calls `check_publishable` under the lease and refuses a commitment whose cut epoch is below the durable floor. #1739 closed that gap on `RootPublish` only.

A second, smaller gap: `reresolve_before_signing` in `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` passes when the fan-out returns no record (`NoUpdate`). The drain then signs the scope root with the section from the start of its pass, with no fresh floor read. That is the shape #1750 closed on `RootPublish`: it fails open on a resolve that gets no answer.

## Fix

- Make `reseal_root` (or `publish_moved` before it) read the cut-epoch floor under the lease and refuse a commitment below it, the same as `RootPublish::check_publishable`.
- Make `reresolve_before_signing` treat `NoUpdate` as a refusal to sign, or re-read the floors before the sign.
- Add a test for each path that raises the cut-epoch floor between the pass start and the sign.

The retroactive ADR 0041 in cipher-box-next records the rule and lists this as residual E1.

Found in the ADR 0041 review of the blueprint commit history on 2026-09-26.

=================== #2021
TITLE: Dead-letter discard, preserved-set trim and refused release send no retire and leak charged registry rows
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: v2-build,comp:engine,post-cutover
MILESTONE: post-cutover

## Problem

Three paths release a charged version and send no retire, so the registry rows the version charged leak with no bound:

- `Engine::discard_dead_letter` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:12648`).
- `trim_preserved`, whose evicted roots `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters` releases (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:517`, `:891`).
- `Drain::release_if_refused` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:6221`), reached from the spent-budget arm of `apply_valve` and from `abandon_keeping_its_name` when the preserved set refuses the version.

Each calls `release_version_blocks` and sends no retire. That drops the only manifest that lists the charged CIDs. Affected: dead letters that keep their rows (a spent attempt budget, `BaseSuperseded`, `AlreadyPublished`, a spent unattributed budget). `Preservation::ContentGone` leaks the same way. This is a leak, not a loss.

## Fix

- Before any of these releases, read the CID set with `version_leaf_cids` plus the root, and hand it to a durable retire that subtracts what the node's live record still names (`live_node_cids`, record-scoped). Then release.
- Do not send a blind account-wide retire. An earlier acknowledged PUT may have left a live record that names the version, and the trim runs outside a drain pass.
- Close two gaps in the retire ledger. The ledger stores only the root and fetches the leaves from the network when it settles, so a root that never uploaded stays owed with no end: store the leaf list or retire inline inside a drain pass. For a create that never published, `OwingRecord::Published` treats the missing record as unreadable and never retires the entry: add the class that treats a missing record as an empty live set.
- Custody: the trim may journal only entries this session's keys can open. It must keep any other entry rather than release it.
- Add a test per path that asserts the retire reaches the fake registry.

The retroactive ADR 0047 in cipher-box-next records the retire rules and lists this as residual E2.

Found in the ADR 0047 review of the blueprint commit history on 2026-09-26.

=================== #1956
TITLE: engine: the owner manual refresh stays reconciling after a write grantee builds inside the folder
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: v2-build,comp:engine
MILESTONE: post-cutover

## Observed

Staging E2E run 35938670706 on the deployed v2.5.0 (2026-09-24 00:29 UTC, dispatched against `https://app-staging.cipherbox.cc`) failed one profile: `tests/web-e2e/staging/writable-share.spec.ts`. The write grantee uploaded a file and created a folder inside the granted folder. Then the owner's page opened the folder and pressed the manual refresh. The status indicator stayed on `data-staleness="reconciling"` for the full 5-minute test timeout, and the click did not complete:

```text
Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 300000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for getByTestId('status-indicator')
    - locator resolved to <button ... data-staleness="reconciling" data-testid="status-indicator">
    - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
  at tests/web-e2e/staging/writable-share.spec.ts:37:35
```

The cause of the wait is unknown. `apps/web/src/components/layout/StatusIndicator.tsx` renders a `<button>` with no `disabled` state, so the button was never disabled. Playwright waited for visibility or stability, or the page did not respond. One hypothesis: the label flips between "synced" and "syncing...", the flip changes the button width, and the width change can block the stability check.

The same profile passed 30 minutes earlier on the same build, in the tag-staging run 35930863688 (3.9 min). The staging host load was about 1.0 on 2 vCPU during the run. The API logged no error, and someguy logged no routing error in the window.

The profile passed again in the tag-staging run 35947080124 (v2.6.0, `48bd33e63`). This pass does not prove a fix. Between `ee147eac9` and `48bd33e63`, only #1944 (a web invite-page change) and the release commit landed.

## What this looks like

An owner sync pass that does not settle after a grantee writes inside a granted folder. The status indicator reports the tick state of the engine, so the stall is below the web shell. The run is one occurrence. The profile passed in the run before it and in the next tag-staging run.

Candidate cause, not proven: the owner and a write grantee derive one name key for the granted folder, so they are two writers of one record. PR #1982 added lost-race rebasing (`Halt::LostRace`): the op stays at the head of the queue, and the next pass rebases and signs above. A run of lost races can keep a pass from settling. No evidence from run 35938670706 ties the stall to this path.

PR #1989 added the expired-link sweep to the tick (`crates/engine/src/facade/link_sweep.rs`). It runs under the `Running` lock on `SyncTimingProfile::link_sweep_cadence`. This is one more tick job. It is not a fix for this issue.

Issue #1880 (a write grantee cannot build inside the granted folder) closed on 2026-09-25. This issue does not depend on it.

## Scope

- Find why a pass can stay in the reconciling state for minutes on the owner side after a grantee write. Read the focus-window tick of the engine and the child resolve for a scope the owner shares with write permission.
- If the pass legitimately waits on the 30 s record-plane deadline several times, make the manual refresh report a failed refresh instead of a reconciling state that never ends.
- Add a gate that fails when a manual refresh stays reconciling past one deadline.

input.prompt:
You are lane A of wave 20 in the CipherBox repo. Your job: fix issues #2016 and #2021 in ONE engine PR, test-first, and open it as a draft.

FIRST read `~/.claude/scratch/w20/common-brief.md` in full and obey it. Your scratch dir is `~/.claude/scratch/w20/2016-2021/`. Your branch: `fix/2016-2021-floor-read-and-retire`.

Then read, in order: `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md` (sections on rotation, epochs, floors, the sync pass, the drain, retire), `decisions/0041-a-rotation-reads-every-floor-again-before-it-seals.md`, `decisions/0047-a-failed-or-abandoned-publish-retires-exactly-what-it-charged.md`, and the two issue bodies below. Use the `mattpocock-skills:tdd` skill: write the failing test for each path first, then the fix.

## Issue #2016 (engine): Write-wave root arm signs a commitment without a cut-epoch floor read

The root arm of the write wave signs a commitment without a read of the cut-epoch floor. `WriteWaveNet::publish_moved` in `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs` (line ~4690) reads the read-epoch floor and the write-epoch floor, then calls `reseal_root` (line ~4575), which re-signs `authorized_commitment` with no cut-epoch floor read. Every other owner publish path reaches the check: the grant-edit publishes go through `OwnerRotationNet::publish_scope_root` and `RootPublish::run`, which calls `check_publishable` (line ~2215) under the lease and refuses a commitment whose cut epoch is below the durable floor.

A second, smaller gap: `reresolve_before_signing` in `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` (line ~5972) passes when the fan-out returns no record (`NoUpdate`). The drain then signs the scope root with the section from the start of its pass, with no fresh floor read. It fails open on a resolve that gets no answer.

Fix:
- Make `reseal_root` (or `publish_moved` before it) read the cut-epoch floor under the lease and refuse a commitment below it, the same as `RootPublish::check_publishable`. A refusal is a `TrustViolation`-class gate rejection, per the AGENTS.md rule.
- Make `reresolve_before_signing` treat `NoUpdate` as a refusal to sign, or re-read the floors before the sign.
- Add a test for each path that raises the cut-epoch floor between the pass start and the sign.
ADR 0041 records the rule and lists this as residual E1.

## Issue #2021 (engine): Dead-letter discard, preserved-set trim and refused release send no retire and leak charged registry rows

Three paths release a charged version and send no retire, so the registry rows the version charged leak with no bound:
- `Engine::discard_dead_letter` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs` line ~10391).
- `trim_preserved` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs` line ~517), whose evicted roots `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters` (line ~861) releases.
- `Drain::release_if_refused` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` line ~6356), reached from the spent-budget arm of `apply_valve` (line ~2008) and from `abandon_keeping_its_name` (line ~6366) when the preserved set refuses the version.
Each calls `release_version_blocks` and sends no retire. That drops the only manifest that lists the charged CIDs. Affected: dead letters that keep their rows (a spent attempt budget, `BaseSuperseded`, `AlreadyPublished`, a spent unattributed budget). `Preservation::ContentGone` leaks the same way. This is a leak, not a loss.

Fix:
- Before any of these releases, read the CID set with `version_leaf_cids` plus the root, and hand it to a durable retire that subtracts what the node's live record still names (`live_node_cids`, record-scoped). Then release.
- Do not send a blind account-wide retire. An earlier acknowledged PUT may have left a live record that names the version, and the trim runs outside a drain pass.
- Close two gaps in the retire ledger (`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs`, seam `crates/engine/src/seams/retire_ledger.rs` with `OwingRecord`). The ledger stores only the root and fetches the leaves from the network when it settles, so a root that never uploaded stays owed with no end: store the leaf list or retire inline inside a drain pass. For a create that never published, `OwingRecord::Published` treats the missing record as unreadable and never retires the entry: add the class that treats a missing record as an empty live set.
- Custody: the trim may journal only entries this session's keys can open. It must keep any other entry rather than release it.
- Add a test per path that asserts the retire reaches the fake registry.
ADR 0047 records the retire rules and lists this as residual E2.

## Lane notes
- If a durable ledger entry shape changes (a stored leaf list), keep entries written by the previous release readable. State the choice in the PR body.
- Lane B (issue #1956) runs in parallel and may edit `sync/drain.rs` around `Halt::LostRace`, `sync/refresh.rs`, `sync/pass.rs`, and `manual_refresh` in the facade. Keep your drain.rs edits scoped to `reresolve_before_signing`, `release_if_refused`, `abandon_keeping_its_name`, and `apply_valve`. The second PR to merge rebases.
- This diff signs commitments, so run `crypto-privacy-review` in addition to `simplify` and `security-review`.
- Commit per issue at minimum (two or more commits), each passing the gates.

Observed: staging E2E run 35938670706 on v2.5.0 failed `tests/web-e2e/staging/writable-share.spec.ts`. The write grantee uploaded a file and created a folder inside the granted folder. One hypothesis: the label flips between "synced" and "syncing...", the width change blocks Playwright's stability check. The same profile passed 30 minutes earlier on the same build and again on v2.6.0 (no engine change between). One occurrence.

What this looks like: an owner sync pass that does not settle after a grantee writes inside a granted folder. The status indicator reports the tick state of the engine, so the stall is below the web shell. Candidate cause, not proven: the owner and a write grantee derive one name key for the granted folder, so they are two writers of one record. 1. Find why a pass can stay in the reconciling state for minutes on the owner side after a grantee write. Read the focus-window tick of the engine and the child resolve for a scope the owner shares with write permission.
2. If the pass legitimately waits on the 30 s record-plane deadline several times, make the manual refresh report a failed refresh instead of a reconciling state that never ends.

Time is injected: the bound must come from a seam or policy value, never a direct clock. Read `SyncTimingProfile` and the existing deadline seams before you add a value.

<result>I found five efficiency issues. Only the first costs anything real, and only on web.

1. **crates/engine/src/sync/tick.rs:523** (`run_past_deadline`, called from facade.rs:5673). A new 30 s timer is started for every pass, including poll, focus and wake passes. Almost every pass finishes in milliseconds, so the timer is nearly always wasted.
   - On desktop, dropping a `tokio::time::sleep` removes it from the timer wheel. That is cheap.
   - On web, the seam just calls `setTimeout(resolve, ms)` (packages/client/src/seams/scheduler.ts:20). `SchedulerAdapter::sleep` (crates/wasm/src/seams_bridge.rs:422) awaits the promise, and dropping it never calls `clearTimeout`.
   - Cost: each pass leaves a timer, a Promise and two wasm-bindgen callback closures alive for the full 30 s. When the timer fires, it calls into wasm to resolve a future nobody is waiting on. The poll cadence (30 s) equals the deadline, so at least one orphan timer is always alive. Focus passes during navigation add more. A throttled background tab holds them longer.
   - Cheaper: return a timer handle from the JS seam and clear it in a Rust `Drop` guard, or pass an `AbortSignal`. Another option is one long-lived overrun timer per tick loop that is re-armed per pass.

   - Cost: two fields kept in sync by hand at three constructors (2385, 2687, the test fixture at 7245), and a hidden invariant a future constructor can break.

2. **`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs:547-563`**: the new `tombstone_of: BTreeMap<[u8;16], bool>` duplicates the existing `tombstoned: BTreeSet<[u8;16]>`. The set is exactly the keys whose value is `true`.
   - Simpler form: keep only the map, and at line 636 take `tombstone_of.iter().filter(|(_, t)| **t).map(|(n, _)| *n)`.
   - Cost: two collections written in the same branch that must stay in step.

**Knock-on complexity from item 1**

3. **`drain.rs:5966-5994`**: the destructure grows from a 6-tuple to a 7-tuple, and rustfmt spreads the binding over 9 lines. `is_scope_root` and `carried_cut_epoch` are both pulled out, then split between two callees. Fixing item 1 brings this back to 6 elements, or you can bind a small struct instead of a positional tuple.

4. **`drain.rs:6029-6060`**: `reresolve_before_signing` now takes one `Option<u64>` that carries both "is scope root" and "the epoch", and needs a doc line to explain that. Its tail went from a 3-line `match` to an `if` plus a second `match`.
   - Simpler form: keep the `bool` parameter and call `refuse_below_cut_floor` from the caller, or from the scope-root branch.
   - Cost: a parameter with two meanings, plus a doc sentence that restates the signature.

**Copy-paste with slight variation**

5. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:4594` and `:10416`**: the same four-argument `DroppedVersionDebts::new(&staging_store, session.enc_subkey(), &*entropy, &content_profile)` is written out twice. `drain.rs` already has a `dropped_version_debts` helper for exactly this.
   - Simpler form: an `Engine::dropped_version_debts(&self, session)` helper, or one that returns `Option<_>` off `self.session`.
   - Cost: two call sites to change whenever the constructor changes.

6. **`drain.rs:6442-6463`**: `release_owing_its_rows` wraps `release_if_refused` and adds only one `if preserved != Kept`. After this PR, `release_if_refused` has one caller left (1951) and the wrapper has three.
   - Simpler form: fold the owe into one function that takes `scope`.
   - Cost: two near-identical functions, and a 5-line doc that lists the `Preservation` variants the code already names.

**Deep nesting and index juggling**

7. **`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs` `trim_preserved` (~590)**: it now returns a `BTreeSet<usize>`, builds `live: Vec<usize>` as the complement, and indexes twice (`sized[live[evicted]].2`). The caller then walks `sized` again with `released.contains(&at)`.
   - Simpler form: return a `Vec<bool>` keep-mask, or partition the tuples into `(kept, dropped)` so the caller only filters `dropped` with `debts.opens`.
   - Cost: an ordered set used for small dense indices, two index levels, and a rescan in the caller.

8. **`staging.rs` `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters` (~966-990)**: `debts: Option<_>` is threaded through, but when it is `None` nothing can be dropped. The function still reads and sizes every entry, then returns at `live.len() == before`. The release loop also re-checks `if let Some(debts) = debts`, which cannot fail once `dropped` has any entries.
   - Simpler form: `let Some(debts) = debts else { return };` at the top, or make the parameter non-`Option` and skip the call at the site.
   - Cost: a `match` on a pair plus a dead re-check, a wasted pass when `debts` is `None`, and the doc sentence "with no `debts` nothing is" exists only to explain this.

**Comments that break the AGENTS.md rules**

9. **`drain.rs` doc on `refuse_below_cut_floor` (~6064)**: "the pass would otherwise sign its pass-start section over a cut it never saw" describes a path that is not in the code, which the AGENTS.md comment rules forbid. The `ADR 0041 D1` citation is enough. The same goes for "`carried_cut_epoch` is `Some` on a scope root" at 6029, which restates the type. On `DroppedVersionDebts::opens` (staging.rs), "A version only this session can journal a debt for is one only it may drop" is a justification for a one-line `classify` pass-through.

**Tests**

10. **`crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` (diff: 1455, 1496, 1593)**: three new tests repeat the same ~15-line prologue: `seed_account`, `device`, `boot`, `refuse_register(proxy_400())`, and `write_file(NewFile{ROOT,..}, 0..200)`, before calling `staged_version`. Two of them also plant the foreign `PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS`.
    - Simpler form: a fixture such as `refused_new_file(&world, &blocks, poison_preserved: bool) -> (alice, engine, tasks, root_cid, leaves)`.
    - Cost: about 45 duplicated lines, and the file already has 8 copies of `refuse_register(proxy_400())`.

11. **`retire.rs` tests (diff: 353-484, 1754-1776)**:
    - `a_dropped_versions_node_is_read_as_unconfirmed` builds the whole `drain_owed_retires` call by hand (ApiClient, RootSource, gateway). That makes 7 hand-built calls in the module. A `drain_with_live(store, http, live)` helper would remove about 25 lines here.
    - `dropped_version` returns `root_block`, which duplicates `entry.dropped_root`.
    - `a_carried_root_that_is_not_the_targets_block_retires_nothing` builds a `dropped_version` only to overwrite `dropped_root`, so `owed_version` would do.
    - `encode_entry(..).expect("the entry encodes")` is repeated three times; an `encoded()` test helper would cover it.</result>

Fix: call `refuse_stale_cut_epoch(&self.authorized_commitment, cut_floor)` and map the error to `Rejected`, or pull out one shared floor check for both arms. 5. **`sync/staging.rs:338` `owe`** reads the root block from the store again (`staged_bytes(root)`). On the reconcile path, `open_version` (`sync/staging.rs:540`) has already read and CID-checked that same block for the same entry. Cost: one extra staged read per dropped version, and a second root-reading path next to `open_version`. This one is minor. Fixing it means passing the block through `sized`, which the diff already reworks.

<result>I found eight altitude issues: three in the cut-floor fix and five in the dead-letter debt work. All paths are under `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a32c3cf79b6d4e92a/crates/engine/src/`.

**(a) Cut-epoch floor before signing**

1. **`net/rotation.rs:4773-4780` and `sync/drain.rs:6066` (`refuse_below_cut_floor`): the same check now exists in three hand-written places.** The PR copies the comparison that `RootPublish::check_publishable` does (`net/rotation.rs:2215`) into two more signers, and each copy maps the failure to a different error. The actual bug was that the check lived in one publish path rather than in the step every scope-root signer goes through.
   - **General fix:** one async precondition in `gate::floor`, something like `root_publishable(floors, scope, read_epoch, write_epoch, cut_epoch)`, taken under the write-epoch lease. Every scope-root signer except genesis provision would call it, or it could wrap `author_scope_root_*`.
   - **Cost:** the next floor, or the next signer, repeats the omission this PR is fixing. The drain copy has already drifted. `check_publishable`'s own doc says the floor read only holds under `acquire_write_epoch_lease`, and `drain.rs` never takes that lease.

2. **`sync/drain.rs:1270-1272` (`FolderState`): two fields say the same thing.** `is_scope_root: bool` now sits next to `carried_cut_epoch: Option<u64>`, and `is_scope_root == carried_cut_epoch.is_some()`. `reresolve_before_signing` branches on the Option, while `publish_node` and `adopt_node_record` (around 6148 and 6243) still branch on the bool.
   - **General fix:** one field, e.g. `scope_root: Option<ScopeRootFacts { cut_epoch, .. }>`.
   - **Cost:** two sources of truth for "is this the scope root" on the signing path, and each new fact about a root adds another parallel field.

3. **`sync/drain.rs:6078-6082`: the drain reports this condition as a trust violation, the rotation paths don't.** The drain builds a `GateRejection { CommitmentVerify, TrustViolation::CommitmentInvalid }` and sends it out through `refuse_record`. The two rotation copies of the same check just return `Rejected`.
   - **Cost:** a benign race, where another leg raised the floor, reaches clients as a trust violation, and the same condition gets different meanings depending on which path signs. A shared precondition (item 1) would give it one verdict.

**(b) Dead-letter registry debts**

4. **`sync/drain.rs:6453`, `facade.rs:10416` and `sync/staging.rs:966-990`: each of the three release paths does "owe, then release" by hand, in its own order.** The facade takes the entry, then owes, then releases. The drain owes, then calls `release_if_refused`. The reconcile writes the list, then owes, then releases. The shared fact is "the staged root block is the only manifest of what was charged," and that belongs to one primitive.
   - **General fix:** a single `drop_version(store, debts, op)` in `sync/staging.rs` that owes and then releases, and that every non-publish caller of `release_version_blocks` goes through.
   - **Cost:** `release_version_blocks` stays a footgun. The failure-valve and residue releases (`drain.rs:2261`, 6497-6508) still bypass it, and the next new release path will too.

5. **`sync/drain.rs:6453` (`release_owing_its_rows`) and `sync/staging.rs:297`: this adds a third mechanism for "rows charged by a version that will never publish."** The existing two are `abandon`'s immediate retire via `registered_by` and `discard_upload`'s immediate retire; this PR adds a deferred ledger journal. It also journals at release time, which is too late for a version whose root is already gone: `owe` does nothing on `Preservation::ContentGone`, even though `release_owing_its_rows` routes that case to it on purpose.
   - **Deeper fix:** journal the debt when the rows are charged (upload/registration) and discharge it when the publish lands.
   - **Cost of the current approach:** three retire policies to keep consistent, and the rows of a ContentGone version still leak. The trade-off of the deeper fix is one ledger write per version upload.

6. **`sync/staging.rs:966-975`: a journaling capability now decides whether the preserved-set bounds are enforced.** `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters` only drops entries that `DroppedVersionDebts::opens` can decrypt. With `debts: None` (no session yet, or a tick with no passes), nothing is trimmed at all. Age, count and byte bounds that used to hold unconditionally now depend on who is signed in.
   - **General fix:** keep trimming independent of the session, and have a foreign or pre-session entry leave a debt the owning session picks up later. Alternatively, key the journal by the entry's owner tag rather than the caller's.
   - **Cost:** the set can grow past `MAX_PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS` and past its byte budget on shared or pre-session stores. `DroppedVersionDebts` also ends up owning a `RecordReader` purely to act as a trim filter.

7. **`seams/retire_ledger.rs:28,60` and `net/retire.rs:564`: one field carries two meanings.** `dropped_root.is_some()` stands for both "where the root block comes from" and "which `OwingRecord` class the node is read under".
   - **General fix:** an explicit origin, e.g. `enum DebtOrigin { Prune, DroppedVersion { root } }`, or store the owing class in the entry.
   - **Cost:** some combinations can't be expressed, such as a prune debt whose root never reached a gateway (it needs the carried root but is Published). The settle's node cache is also now keyed by `(node, class)`, so a node owing both kinds of debt is read twice.

8. **`net/retire.rs:409-429`: the ledger format is versioned by a tag tacked on after the CID, and it now holds whole root blocks.** Decoding depends on "every well-formed CID is one length" for disambiguation, instead of the entry grammar carrying a version byte. It also breaks the ledger's stated design ("three orders of magnitude smaller than the CID set"): entries now hold root blocks up to `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES`, and every `owed()` page loads them.
   - **General fix:** a versioned entry header. For the root itself, either keep the staged root block pinned in staging under a key the ledger references, or upload it.
   - **Cost:** the next extension needs another trailing-tag trick, and ledger size and per-pass read cost now grow with dead-letter root size.</result>

<result>I found seven places where the diff adds wasted work, listed from highest to lowest cost. All paths are under `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a32c3cf79b6d4e92a/crates/engine/src/`, and line numbers are from the worktree.

1. **`sync/drain.rs:5460-5476` + `:5491-5503`: a second fan-out resolve in `holds_no_record`, then `load_child_node`.** For an `Unconfirmed` node whose record does exist (the usual case: a dead letter on a file that was published before), `holds_no_record` makes a full `fanout_get_classified` round trip to every endpoint. It then comes back `Present`, and the code goes on to `load_scope_root` plus a NoCache `load_child_node` fan-out on the same name. It also reads the sequence floor, which the child gate reads again.
   - Cost: one extra network fan-out and one extra floor read per `Unconfirmed` node per settle pass.
   - Cheaper: call `load_child_node` first and apply the "absent and never adopted" rule only when it reports no record. Or hand the `FanoutRecord::Present` bytes from the classified fetch to the gate so the name is only fetched once.

2. **`net/retire.rs:569` (`live_of` keyed by `(node, OwingRecord)`): the same node's live set is computed twice.** A node that has both prune debts (`Published`) and dropped-version debts (`Unconfirmed`) gets two full `live_owing_record` runs. That means two scope-root resolves, two child NoCache resolves, and a gateway `read_block` and expand for every pinned version, done twice. `Unconfirmed` only differs from `Published` when `holds_no_record` is true.
   - Cost: up to double the network reads per such node per settle.
   - Cheaper: cache the live set per node. Work out `Unconfirmed` as "empty if no record is held, otherwise the cached `Published` set".

3. **`sync/staging.rs:954` → `:987` (`owe`) → `:988` (`release_version_blocks`): the staged root block is read three times per trimmed entry.** `open_version` reads, `verify_cid`s and decodes the root. Then `owe` re-reads it at `:338`, and `expand_staged_root` verifies and decodes it again. Then `version_leaf_cids` reads, verifies and decodes it a third time.
   - Cost: 3× (staging read of up to 2 MiB, SHA-256, det-CBOR decode) per dropped version, where 1× would do.
   - Cheaper: keep the root block (or manifest) from `open_version` in `sized`, pass it to `owe` to expand from the bytes, and release the leaves from that same manifest.

4. **`sync/drain.rs:6453-6463` and `facade.rs:10408-10427`: the root block is read twice on the dead-letter and discard paths.**
   - `owe` reads, verifies and decodes the root. Then `release_if_refused` / `release_version_blocks` reads, verifies and decodes it again.
   - On `Preservation::ContentGone`, `preserve_dead_letter` has already found the root gone (`staging.rs:461`), yet `owe` still issues a `staged_bytes` read that returns `None`.
   - Cheaper: one "journal then release" helper that reads the root once and returns the leaf CIDs. Skip `owe` when the root is already known to be gone.

5. **`sync/staging.rs:313` (`DroppedVersionDebts::new` → `RecordReader::new` → `enc_secret.public()`): an X25519 base-point multiply on every construction.**
   - The settle already works out `owner_tag(vault.enc_secret)` at `drain.rs:1816`, and the comment there says it is done once for this reason. `drain.rs:1861` then rebuilds it through `dropped_version_debts(vault)`.
   - `drain.rs:1725` builds it again on every non-vault tick, `drain.rs:6460` on every dead letter, and `facade.rs:4594` / `facade.rs:10416` do the same.
   - Cost: one extra scalar multiply per tick, plus one per dead letter.
   - Cheaper: have `DroppedVersionDebts` take the owner tag the caller already has (or a `RecordReader` built once), and build it once per tick.

6. **`sync/staging.rs:941-979`: per-tick preserved-set sizing whose result is thrown away.**
   - When `debts` is `None` (the `run_tick` branch at `drain.rs:1723` with no passes, or facade startup with no session), nothing can be dropped. Even so, `read_preserved_dead_letters`, one `open_version` root read per entry, and `trim_preserved` all still run before `live.len() == before` returns.
   - Entries `opens` rejects (another identity's records) are now kept for good. Every tick re-sizes them (a root read each) and re-runs `classify` (ECDH + AEAD) on them, with no chance of them ever being dropped.
   - Cheaper: return right after the orphan sweep when `debts` is `None`. Remember the entries that could not be opened (for example, by op id for the session) so later ticks stop re-classifying them.

7. **`net/retire.rs:170-230` (`encode_entry` / `decode_entry` carrying `dropped_root`): whole root blocks stored in the ledger and unsealed on every settle page.** `owed()` unseals and copies every entry's carried root block (up to 2 MiB each, up to `MAX_BOOKKEEPING_OPENS` = 256 per page). That happens even for entries that are only counted or deferred, and again on every tick until the entry settles.
   - Cost: extra AEAD work and allocation on every settle tick, growing with the size of the stuck entries.
   - Cheaper: store the carried root under its own key and read it lazily in `expand_owed`, only when the entry is actually about to be expanded.

On the scope-root sign path I found only minor costs:
- **`sync/drain.rs:6057-6076` (`refuse_below_cut_floor`):** one local floor read per scope-root publish. It is small next to the NoCache fan-out before it, and it has to come after the re-resolve, so it cannot run in parallel. When the resolve did return a record, the gate probably read the same cut floor already, so passing that value out would save the read.
- **`net/rotation.rs:4775`:** the cut-floor read comes straight after the write-floor read. It is two sequential local reads once per rotation, which is negligible, but they could be read together if the floors API allows it.</result>

input.message:
All four simplify results are in (they route to the orchestrator). Below: the orchestrator's decisions first, then the raw findings. Fold, then finish the lane (crypto-privacy-review, security-review, code-review, gates, one push, one CI wait, final report). Do not stop before the final report.

## Diagnosis

The report artifact of run 35938670706 shows both grantee rows in the owner's listing. The footer shows "syncing...". So the owner pass reconciled the grantee's writes. The indicator was wrong after the data landed.

- **Mechanism 1 (found, this is the cause):** `status()` and `snapshot()` compute the staleness rung when the host reads it. A read during a pass returns `Reconciling`. After the pass, `stamp_staleness` sent `StalenessChanged` only when the rung differed from the last *event*, not from the last read. After a converged pass the rung is `Fresh` again, so no event went out. The web store reads the rung during a pass: on each `SnapshotUpdated` pull, and when `manualRefresh` resolves. So it kept `reconciling`, and no later event replaced it. A test holds the root read and reads the rung during the pass. On main it gets no event after the pass converges.
- **Mechanism 2 (found):** the manual refresh and the `Reconciling` rung had no time bound. A test shows that on main a refresh on a stalled pass stays pending past 30 s. The run gives no proof that a pass actually waited on the record deadlines.
- **Ruled out:** the lost-race loop. `Halt::LostRace` ends the drain for that pass. `UNATTRIBUTED_BUDGET` (120) limits the retries for each op. The test gave the owner no write in that window.
- **Not explained:** Playwright waited on "visible, enabled and stable" and never clicked. A rung that does not change does not change the button box. The engine harness cannot reproduce this.
- **Partial:** scope item 1 asked me to read the focus-window tick and the child resolve for a scope shared with write permission. I did not write up that read. The artifact shows the child resolve delivered both rows.

## What the PR does

- **Rung read recorded:** a host read of the rung records it as `SyncStatus::reported` (`SyncStatus::observe`). The pass that ends that rung then sends the next rung.
- **New bound:** `SyncTimingProfile::refresh_deadline` is 30 s in both profiles, one host record-request deadline. All timing comes from one clock: the pass start, which the tick loop records in `reconcile_started`.
- **Bounded rung:** `classify` shows `Reconciling` for one deadline only. After that it shows `Fresh` or `Stale` from the last success.
- **Rung changes during a pass:** `run_with_boundaries` wakes at each time `staleness::next_boundary` returns. It sends the new rung and lets the pass continue. It never cancels the pass.
- **Overdue refresh:** at the deadline, `ManualRefresh::overdue` sends the new `RefreshVerdict::Overdue` to every waiting request, and to each request filed later in that tick. `ForcedPass::landed` maps `Overdue` to `RefreshFailed`. The web command, the desktop path and the other `file_forced_pass` callers all get the bound.
- **Gates:** three Engine-harness tests in `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`:
  - A read during the pass is replaced by an event when the pass converges.
  - A forced refresh on a stalled pass fails at the deadline, and in the same instant the host gets a rung other than `Reconciling`.

**Scope `Overdue` to the settled pass.**
`settle_verdict` answers the current pass before `assemble_scopes` runs its drain. The boundary callback can then call `ManualRefresh::overdue()` during that drain. Because `overdue()` answers `queued`, a request filed after `settle` can receive `RefreshVerdict::Overdue` even though it is queued for the next pass. `filed()` also pre-answers later requests while `inner.overdue` remains set.
Track the settled-pass boundary so `overdue()` and `filed()` fail only requests owned by the overdue pass. Requests filed after `settle` must remain queued for the next pass. Preserve the existing behavior for requests waiting behind an unsettled poll pass.

<result>I found no loss path in the fold for the case it targets. I found one real residual: the Edit rule compares only the head CID, and the next publish can reuse the same sequence number. That residual can still cause loss.

## Findings

### MEDIUM: a version from an unconfirmed edit can still surface at a sequence another record now holds (real, narrow)

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` in `live_owing_record` (line 5498), in the head publish (`min_current_sequence: None` at line 6308, `Unconfirmed => Err(Halt::Attempt)` at line 6325), and in `resolved_bytes` (line 7106), which drops `tied`.

**Description:** An endpoint acknowledges the PUT of edit E at sequence N+1 but does not confirm it. The sequence floor stays at N. The version is dropped, and the user edits again. The new record Y also signs at N+1. If no endpoint serves E yet, Y confirms. The settle then reads head Y, and Y is not the base B. So the entry reads as `Published` and the settle retires E's CIDs. The background re-PUT (`spawn_background_reput`) can still put E on an endpoint that missed Y or refused it at the same sequence. `load_child_node` takes one record from a tie and ignores the others. A reader with floor N whose first endpoint serves E adopts E, and E's content is already unpinned.

The same gap applies to your case of `Edit(None)` when the node has later versions, and to a record from another writer at N+1.

**Impact:** Loss for new devices and share recipients. You need a lagging endpoint plus a refused or missed PUT at the same sequence. Honest endpoints can get there. A hostile endpoint gets there easily.

**Recommendation:**
- Record the acknowledged sequence S in the entry, for example `DroppedFrom::Edit { base, acked_seq }`, or keep a durable "acked-high" mark for each name.
- Pass `min_current_sequence = S` on the next publish of that name, so it signs strictly above E.
- In the settle, return `None` (wait) while the gated sequence is at or below S, or while `tied` is not empty. This rule does the job the head-CID check does now, and it does not depend on the base.

### LOW: the Edit rule can wait forever (leak, not loss)

**Location:** the same check at `drain.rs:5498`.

**Description:** A record above N+1 whose head is B again stands the entry down for good. A prune, a RestoreVersion, or a lazy-wave re-seal can make such a record. The stall reason says `NodeUnreadable`, which is wrong. The sequence rule above fixes this too.

### INFO: unjournaled debts are silent

**Location:** `net/retire.rs` `acknowledged`.

**Location:** `publish_node`, the `Unconfirmed` arm.

**Description:** If `acknowledge` fails, the halt is `Unclassified`, not `Attempt`. If the op dead-letters on a rebase before it publishes again, no mark exists, and a later local record can sign N+1 again. The loss also needs the staging store to fail right after the PUT.

- **Secret logging:** none.
- **Comments:** short. The only drift is the `Halt::Attempt` comment above.

The pass-region wave from the handoff is complete. All three PRs are merged, the four issues are closed, and main is green.

**Merged today, in order:**

- PR 2059 for issue 2017. The desktop shell forces a sync pass on a network reconnect and on a wake from sleep. One sampler thread reads the wall clock and the routable networks every 5 s, on all three platforms.
- PR 2060 for issue 1956. The lane found the cause: a rung the host read during a pass was never followed by an event after the pass converged, so the web store kept `reconciling`. The fix records every read, bounds the manual refresh and the `Reconciling` rung by one 30 s refresh deadline from the pass start, and fails a stalled refresh with a new overdue verdict.
- PR 2063 for issues 2016 and 2021. One gate helper holds every scope-root signer to the cut-epoch floor. One drop primitive journals what a dropped dead-letter version charged before its release. The retire ledger entry is versioned and carries the target set, the previous release entry still decodes, and the drain holds an acknowledged sequence so a dropped record cannot resurface at a sequence a later record confirmed at.

**Checks.** CI was green on each PR. CodeRabbit found no actionable item on PR 2059, two on PR 2060, and one on PR 2063. I rejected those three in the threads with the mechanism, because each described a documented design choice. The post-merge check on main at be3d181da passed clippy and 2800 engine tests.

**Cleanup.** I removed the three lane worktrees and 37 stale placeholder branches from earlier agent worktrees. The T3 worktree on the staging-soak branch belongs to another thread, so I left it.

**Open for you:**

- ADR 0047 amendment. PR 2063 added two durable shapes: the versioned ledger entry grammar and the acknowledged-sequence mark under `cbx/ra/`. Both are candidates for an ADR item.
- Two one-line document gaps from PR 2060. `blueprint/engine.md` "Staleness ladder" does not say `Reconciling` lasts at most one refresh deadline, and `CONTEXT.md` "Manual refresh" does not name the overdue failure. I left both for your blueprint process.
- The drain signs a scope root without the write-epoch lease. The PR 2063 body gives the reasons, chief among them that ADR 0041 E2 says the lease does not stop a cut raise.
- Follow-up issue 2065 covers a dropped version whose staged root is already gone, with the charge-time journal as the candidate design.

# Architecture decision records

An ADR records one architecture decision for CipherBox v2, with its context and its consequences.
Each ADR is one file. The file name has the form `NNNN-<title-as-a-sentence>.md`.
The header of each file gives the status: Proposed, Accepted, Accepted on <date>, or Implemented.
An ADR that amends an older ADR adds an "Amended by" sentence at the amended item in the older file.
Each decision item must pass three hurdles: it is hard to reverse, it is not clear without context, and it is the result of a real trade-off.
If no item passes all three, the ADR is not written.
A test duty, an accepted residual, a deferral, or the bug before a fix is not a decision.
For the full bar and the process that adds or accepts an ADR, read "ADR Process" in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md).
The wayfinder threads and the as-built v1 spec corpus stay in the archived
[FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next). That repo is read-only.

1:# ADR 0047 — A failed or abandoned publish retires exactly what it charged
2:
3:- **Status:** Accepted on 2026-09-26 — retroactive; the rule shipped in FSM1/cipher-box#923,
4:  FSM1/cipher-box#944, FSM1/cipher-box#1046 and FSM1/cipher-box#1862, and the blueprint carries
5:  it; the `blueprint/*.md` and
6:  `CONTEXT.md` rewording in FSM1/cipher-box follows; trimmed on 2026-09-26 to the items that pass
7:  the three ADR hurdles — the removed items live in the blueprint
8:- **Date:** 2026-09-26
9:- **Relates to:**
10:  [#34](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/34) D2 (register-first, fail-closed), D3
11:  (per-account rows, union liveness) and D4 (retire = remove my row; the timing is client
12:  policy), [#24](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/24) D6 (coverage is structural;
13:  retirement is inventory removal), [#33](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/33) D6
14:  (a dead letter keeps its staged bytes),
15:  [#26](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/26) D6 (a fresh random content key per
16:  version),
17:  [ADR 0007](./0007-derived-idempotent-first-run-mint.md)
18:  D4 (the accepted one-head-block crash leak),
19:  [ADR 0011](./0011-quarantine-release-rests-on-the-doomed-manifest.md)
20:  D4 and its Context (no pass that journals an entry may decide it),
21:  [ADR 0019](./0019-file-version-retention-is-count-based-keep-latest-n.md)
22:  D3 and D4 (a retained version stays referenced by its own entry),
23:  [ADR 0046](./0046-the-registry-counts-references-per-record-and-caps-every-batch-at-1000.md)
24:  D1, D2 and E4 (the per-record reference count, the two retire forms, and why these retires use
25:  the account-wide form), the decision of 2026-08-20
26:  on FSM1/cipher-box#1226 (a spent attempt budget keeps the bytes), the `blueprint/engine.md`
27:  "Resolve/publish pipeline" section ("Retirement" bullet), the "Content plane" section
28:  ("Referenced equals kept" bullet) and the "Sync core" dead-letter paragraph, the
29:  `blueprint/api.md` "Pin/name registry" section ("Batch bounds", "Register-first,
30:  fail-closed" and "Per-referencing-record refcount"), and the `CONTEXT.md` "Register-first",
31:  "Union liveness", "Dead-letter" and "Version history" terms
32:- **Implemented by:** FSM1/cipher-box#923 (the abandoned op retires every charged block, D1 and
33:  D2), FSM1/cipher-box#944 (the per-attempt orphaned-head retire, D3 and D4),
34:  FSM1/cipher-box#1046 (the same retire for the vault settings publish),
35:  FSM1/cipher-box#1762 (a name wave carries every version's root and leaves to the new name, D5)
36:  and FSM1/cipher-box#1862 (retained roots register again on each publish, D5).
37:
38:## Context
39:
40:Every block that a publish uploads is its own charged pin row, which the quota gate counts. A
41:record publish uploads its head block through the same charged ingress, and each retry authors a
42:new head under a fresh seal nonce. Before FSM1/cipher-box#944, no path retired an orphaned head,
43:so an op that retried three times and then succeeded leaked three charged heads. The retire is
44:destructive: the registry unpins a CID when its global reference count reaches zero. An op whose
45:record PUT was acknowledged may already be resolvable at its name, so a retire there turns a quota
46:leak into content loss. A fan-out that no endpoint acknowledged does not prove that no endpoint
47:stored the record. A retained file version must stay referenced, or orphan GC collects its root,
48:and the drop of a version cannot be undone.
49:
50:## Decision
51:
52:**D2 — An op whose record PUT was acknowledged retires nothing.** The record may be resolvable at
53:its name. Unpinning content that a live record still references is loss, and leaving the rows
54:charged is only a leak. So a spent attempt budget on an acknowledged-but-unconfirmed publish
55:(`Halt::Attempt`) dead-letters the op and retires neither the name nor a block. An unattributable
56:upload refusal, which fails before any PUT, is a separate halt, `Halt::UploadAttempt`.
57:
58:**D3 — A publish that fails before its record reaches the transport retires its head block, on
59:each attempt.** Such a failure leaves a head block that is already uploaded and charged, and no
60:record can name it. The retry authors a new head under a fresh seal nonce, so the old head is
61:permanently unreachable. The qualifying failures are exactly those that `orphaned_head`
62:(`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs`) names, and it matches every publish error variant
63:exhaustively, so a new variant does not compile until someone classifies it. The engine retires
64:the pending set at the end of the pass that orphaned it, independent of the op's fate: an op that
65:later succeeds still retires what its failed attempts charged. The pending set (`OrphanHeads`) is
66:session-lived and capped at 1000 entries. In the drain, a head that the live held set still names
67:never enters it. The vault settings publish and the bin index publish use the same predicate.
68:
69:**D4 — A fan-out that acknowledged nothing does not qualify under D3.** `AllEndpointsFailed` says
70:that no endpoint acknowledged the PUT. It does not say that no endpoint stored the record. A lost
71:ack can leave a record resolvable at the name that points at this head, and D2's reason applies.
72:
73:**D5 — Each publish of a file registers every retained version's root again under the file's own
74:name, and a dropped version's debt is journaled before the shortened history publishes.** A
75:write-rotation name wave registers every version's root and leaves at the node's new name before
76:the record moves. A version that falls outside the retention rule loses its reference, and what it
77:owes the registry goes to the durable retire ledger first. A debt that the ledger does not take
78:leaves the history standing, and the pass publishes no shortened history. This is the mechanism
79:behind ADR 0019 D3: the entry is the reference, and the re-registration is how the registry
80:learns it.
81:
82:Item D1 moved to `blueprint/engine.md` "Resolve/publish pipeline" ("Retirement" bullet) and
83:`blueprint/api.md` "Pin/name registry" on 2026-09-26.
84:
85:## Alternatives rejected
86:
87:- **Route the whole attempt arm through the abandonment (D2).** The arm included the
88:  acknowledged-but-unconfirmed publish, so the change would unpin a version that a live record may
89:  name. The arm was split instead.
90:- **Keep a durable per-op list of every head the op minted, and retire it at abandonment (D3).**
91:  It misses an op that retries and then succeeds, and it needs a new staging key, a format tag and
92:  a pruning pass. The per-pass retire covers strictly more.
93:- **Re-PUT the bytes of the earlier attempt instead of authoring a new head (D3).** Reuse needs
94:  durable record bytes and a publish plan pinned across passes. The drain re-derives its plan from
95:  the current gate-passing base on each pass, so this is a change to the publish pipeline.
96:- **Retire the head on `AllEndpointsFailed` (D4).** A lost ack leaves a resolvable record that
97:  names the head, so the retire would make that node unreadable.
98:- **Keep a retained version by a separate reference count on its root (D5).** ADR 0019 rejected
99:  this. The version's entry in the read-body is the reference.
100:
101:## Rationale
102:
103:- **D2, D4:** a retire too few is a bounded leak, and a retire too many is a loss that no later
104:  pass can undo, so the engine keeps a row that a live record may name.
105:- **D3:** a failure before the transport means that no record names the head, and the fresh nonce
106:  means that no later record of this op names it; a per-pass retire needs no new durable format.
107:- **D5:** the entry is the reference and the re-registration tells the registry; journal first
108:  makes the drop crash-safe.
109:
110:## Consequences
111:
112:1. `blueprint/engine.md` "Resolve/publish pipeline" ("Retirement") and "Content plane"
113:   ("Referenced equals kept") carry every item, kept and moved.
114:2. `blueprint/api.md` "Pin/name registry" carries the batch cap and the retire forms, and
115:   `CONTEXT.md` "Register-first" and "Version history" define the rows the retire removes.

## Context

A dead letter that keeps its rows — a spent attempt budget, `BaseSuperseded`, `AlreadyPublished`,
a spent unattributed budget — holds a staged version whose registry rows stay charged. Three paths
later drop that version: the member discards the dead letter, the drain's valve refuses or loses
the preserved entry, and the preserved-set trim evicts it. Before FSM1/cipher-box#2063 each of
them released the staged blocks and sent no retire, so the rows leaked with no bound (ADR 0047
E4). The staged root is the only manifest that lists those rows, and it may never have reached a
gateway, so the retire ledger's prune shape — the root alone, leaves fetched at settle time —
cannot carry the debt. ADR 0047 D2 still holds: an acknowledged PUT may be resolvable at its name,
and a later record at the same sequence can lose a tie to it. So the debt may settle only once no
endpoint can still serve the dropped version as the node's live record.

## Decision

**D1 — A dropped version's debt carries its whole target set, in a versioned ledger entry.** The
retire-ledger entry gains a version byte and an origin. A prune debt keeps the root-only shape. A
dropped-version debt lists every leaf and then the root, each with its pinned bytes, so the settle
expands it with no gateway read. Encode refuses a set that is empty, does not end at the root, or
does not sum to the total, and decode reads the same bytes as unwritten (AGENTS.md rule 8). The
unversioned entry the previous release wrote still decodes, as a prune debt. The previous release
reads a versioned entry as unwritten, and the ledger never discards, so such an entry waits for
this release.

**D2 — The drain holds the acknowledged sequence of a PUT that did not confirm, signs above it,
and settles nothing at or below it.** A publish whose PUT was acknowledged but not confirmed, or
that lost a tie at its own sequence, records that sequence for the node under a sealed owner-local
key. The next publish at that name signs strictly above the mark. The settle of a dropped-version
debt reads the node's live record under a new class, `OwingRecord::Unconfirmed`: it waits while the
gated record is at or below the mark, while the endpoints serve other bytes at the same sequence,
or while a mark exists that will not read. A confirmed publish above the mark removes it. A mark
that will not read stands for any sequence, so the publish signs above the sequence floor plus the
attempt budget.

**D3 — A name with no record reads as an empty live set only on unanimous vacancy.** For a
dropped create, the settle treats the name as holding nothing only when every endpoint answers that
it holds no record, this device holds no sequence floor for the name, and no acknowledged-sequence
mark exists for the node. Any other read waits.

## Alternatives considered

- **Retire inline in the drain pass, with no ledger entry (D1).** The discard and the trim run
  outside a pass, and a retire needs the live record's CID set, which only a gated read gives. The
  ledger is the crash-safe carrier the prune already uses.
- **Store the root block in the entry (D1).** Every settle page would unseal roots of up to the
  record ceiling, and the ledger would grow with dead-letter roots. The target set is bounded by
  the manifest.
- **Compare the settle's head against the dropped edit's base (D2).** A later record at the same
  sequence hides the dropped one, and a prune or a restore that makes the head equal the base
  again stalls the debt for good. The sequence mark does not depend on the base.
- **Journal the rows when they are charged, at upload (D1, D2).** It gives the content-gone case
  its rows back, at one ledger write per version upload. Deferred; FSM1/cipher-box#2065 holds it.

## Consequences

1. `blueprint/engine.md` "Retirement" carries the carve-out on the acknowledged-PUT rule: a
   dropped dead-letter version journals its rows and settles above the acknowledged sequence.
2. `blueprint/engine.md` "Referenced equals kept" says that a dropped version's debt carries its
   target set.
3. ADR 0047 D2 reads with D2 here as its limit, and ADR 0047 E4 narrows to the content-gone case.
4. One new owner-local key prefix, `cbx/ra/`, sealed under the retire-ledger kind. The key names
   the owner tag and the node, as the tombstone key does, and the value is sealed.

## Residuals

**E1 — A version whose staged root is already gone journals nothing.** `Preservation::ContentGone`
has no manifest to read, so its rows stay charged. FSM1/cipher-box#2065 names the charge-time
journal as the candidate.

**E2 — A mark outlives a rotation.** The mark is read against the current write name, so a mark
held for an old name reads as nothing and stays as one key per node until a confirmed publish
removes it.

**E3 — Another publisher can tie the dropped record.** A rotation re-seal or a liveness re-sign
does not read the mark. The settle sees the tie and waits, so the exposure is a delay, not a loss.

# ADR 0055 — A manual refresh fails after one record-request deadline, and the pass runs on

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-09-27
- **Relates to:**
  [ADR 0044](./0044-the-engine-owns-refresh-forcing-mailbox-transport-and-the-staging-budget.md)
  D1 (every forced pass goes through `Command::ManualRefresh`) and D2 (a refresh it could not land
  is a failure, not a repaint), [#33](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/33) D3
  (nocache) and D4 (the staleness ladder), the `blueprint/engine.md` "Sync core" section
  ("Staleness ladder" bullet), and the `CONTEXT.md` "Sync pass" and "Manual refresh" terms
- **Implemented by:** FSM1/cipher-box#2060 (closes FSM1/cipher-box#1956)
- **Amends:** ADR 0044 D2

## Context

ADR 0044 D2 names two ends for a manual refresh: what it landed, or a failure. A pass that stalls
on the record plane had a third: no end. `manual_refresh` awaited the pass with no bound, and the
`Reconciling` rung held while the pass ran. Staging run 35938670706 showed the owner's indicator on
`reconciling` for five minutes after a write grantee built inside a shared folder. The pass had in
fact reconciled the grantee's writes. A rung the host read during the pass was never replaced,
because the engine sent a rung change only against the last event it sent, not against the last
rung the host read. Both the refresh and the rung needed a bound. The open questions were which
clock measures it, and what happens to the pass at the bound.

## Decision

**D1 — The waiting refresh and the `Reconciling` rung are bounded by one host record-request
deadline, timed from the pass start, and the pass is not cancelled.**
`SyncTimingProfile::refresh_deadline` equals one record GET or PUT deadline, which neither profile
compresses: a pass that waits on more than one record request has stalled, not reconciled slowly.
At the deadline the tick loop answers every request waiting on the pass, and every request filed
until the tick ends, with `RefreshVerdict::Overdue`, which the host receives as
`EngineError::RefreshFailed`. The ladder stops reading `Reconciling` at the same instant and reads
from the last success. The pass runs to its own end: a pass cut mid-drain would strand what it had
half published, and a later refresh may still land.

## Alternatives considered

- **A clock per request, from its filing time.** A request filed late in a stalled pass would
  wait one full deadline more than the indicator, and the refresh and the rung would leave
  `Reconciling` at different moments. One bound would need three clocks.
- **Cancel the pass at the deadline.** The drain publishes in steps, and a cancelled pass strands
  what it had half published.
- **Several deadlines before the failure.** One record request is the unit the host already
  bounds. A pass that waits on a second one is stalled, and a stall reported after several
  deadlines is a `reconciling` state that lasts minutes.
- **Bound the wait in the host.** The host cannot tell a slow pass from a stalled one, and the
  engine owns refresh forcing (ADR 0044 D1).

## Consequences

1. `blueprint/engine.md` "Staleness ladder" says that `reconciling` lasts at most one
   record-request deadline from the pass start, and that the pass runs on.
2. `CONTEXT.md` "Manual refresh" names the overdue failure as the third way a refresh ends.
3. ADR 0044 D2 reads with D1 here: a pass past the deadline answers `RefreshFailed` too.
4. A rung the host reads counts as reported, so the pass that ends it sends the next rung, and the
   host's own dedup drops a repeat.
5. The tick loop wakes at each rung boundary while a pass runs, so the stale threshold is also
   reported during a long pass.

## Residuals

**E1 — A cold cache stays `Reconciling` past the deadline.** The ladder has no other rung without
a last success, and the refresh itself fails at the deadline.

**E2 — The web scheduler seam has no cancel.** A per-pass deadline timer outlives a short pass on
web. About two such timers are alive at once at the poll cadence.

**E3 — The engine deadline and the host record deadline are two values.** They name each other in
comments and are both 30 s. A host that tunes its record timeout must tune the profile too.
EOF
wc -l decisions/0055-*.md; python3 - <<'PY'
p='decisions/0044-the-engine-owns-refresh-forcing-mailbox-transport-and-the-staging-budget.md'
s=open(p).read()
old="renders the failure over that view. It does not render a success from cached bytes. The rule\nlanded with FSM1/cipher-box#1212; this ADR records it.\n"

old="`FuseOpCore::refresh_hint`, which records the stale node, is read only by tests.\n"
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old, old.rstrip("\n")+" FSM1/cipher-box#2059\nclosed this on 2026-09-27: the desktop shell samples the wall clock and the routable networks\nevery 5 s, and files a forced pass on a wake from sleep and on a network reconnect.\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='blueprint/engine.md'
s=open(p).read()

open(p,'w').write(s)
p='CONTEXT.md'
s=open(p).read()
old="an unreachable record fails it, a rejected one is a trust violation.\n"
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,"an unreachable record fails it, a rejected one is a trust violation, and a pass that runs past one record-request deadline fails it as overdue while the pass runs on (ADR 0055).\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='decisions/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
i=s.index("| [0052](./0052-"); j=s.index("\n",i)
new="| [0055](./0055-a-manual-refresh-fails-after-one-record-request-deadline-and-the-pass-runs-on.md) | A manual refresh fails after one record-request deadline, and the pass runs on | Proposed |"
s=s[:j+1]+new+"\n"+s[j+1:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("edits ok")
PY
